headline: Yoshioka reports agent-designed SAR ADC and independent post-layout checks
fact: Kentaro Yoshioka's arXiv preprint reports an experiment in which LLM agents wrote schematic and layout generators for an 11-bit, 5.12-MS/s SAR ADC on SKY130 and iterated through simulation, DRC, LVS and parasitic extraction. Its reference-assisted condition met the paper's post-extraction criteria after receiving fixed human-supplied inputs, without additional intervention. An independent supervising agent recomputed performance and found false passes, including extraction and connectivity problems. The reported result is a design-flow experiment and simulated sign-off, not measured silicon or a claim that an entire SoC was demonstrated.

sources.title: The Era of Vibe Tapeout: Dark Age or Golden Age for Analog Circuit Design? — arXiv preprint
sources.summary: The October 11 preprint and its indexed full-text view describe the SKY130 SAR ADC experiment, agent-written generators, independent re-verification and false-pass examples. The full-text view was readable through the arXiv search index; a direct page fetch was blocked during this check.
